newsitem.title: UK: Slim Euro oil refinery turnarounds seen this sprin.
newsitem.headline: Slim Euro oil refinery turnarounds seen this sprin.

text.p: European spring oil refinery maintenance turnarounds are likely to remove some 500,000 barrels a day (bpd) of crude distillation capacity, about the same as last year, industry analysts and oil company officials said.

"At the moment it looks like maintenance levels will be little different, but it would only take a few last minute turnarounds for us to see heavier maintenance," said an analyst at a major European refiner.
Maintenance levels in Europe are expected to be little changed, repeating last year's light season after a heavy schedule of repairs in 1995.
"At the moment I don't see any blips in levels that could effect price," said a European products trader.
European refinery capacity is already being trimmed by upcoming closures in Denmark, the Netherlands, Britain and Germany.
Crude throughput lost to maintenance is difficult to predict given the diverse methods of calculation used by oil companies and analysts.
Estimates for the volumes likely to be shutdown in Europe in March due to refinery work this spring ranged from 330,000 to 700,000 barrels per day.
Although refining margins have deteriorated over the past month, most analysts dismissed the possibility of a repeat of 1995 when poor margins led to an abnormally high volume of closures.

"Margins aren't as bad as they were back in 1995 when we saw the exceptionally high level of turnarounds," said Colin Birch of analysts Purvin and Gertz in London. "They've weakened over the past month but they haven't reached the same level."
He saw maintenance levels as being similar to last spring.
Belgian Petrofina said European margins last year rose 47 cents to $2.27 a barrel. French Total SA said its margins went up 31 cents to $1.87.
Scheduled spring maintenance in northwest Europe include total shutdowns at Wintershell's 77,000 bpd Lingen plant in April and BRC's 85,000 bpd Antwerp refinery for three weeks at the end of April.

In France, Elf Aquitaine's 120,000 bpd Feyzin refinery will undergo crude distillation unit (CDU) work in April. The company's 211,000 bpd Donge refinery will be shut for three weeks from February 10. Shell's Berre L'Etang CDU is out for for 12 days from the end of March.
In Britain the 120,000 bpd Milford Haven plant jointly run by Elf UK and Murphy Oil Corp's Murco will be shutdown for six weeks from the end of February.
The 178,000 bpd Coryton refinery jointly run by British Petroleum Plc and Mobil will undergo CDU maintenance for about ten days in March.

In the Mediterranean, works includes total shutdowns at Agip's 90,000 bpd Venice refinery in April and acatalytic cracker and visbreaker shutdown at its 230,000 bpd Priolo refinery in February and March.
